# ReadFromWriteOnlyStream

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Open the stream with read access.

## Example

Finding:

```php{2}
<?php
$fp = fopen($path, "w"); if ($fp === false) { return; } fread($fp, 8);
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Open the stream with read access.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- D1. Track successful fopen with literal w/a/x/c mode and no plus. Report fread, fgets, fgetc, fgetcsv, stream_get_contents or fpassthru receiving that handle before close/reopen.
- D2. Resolve builtin functions, classes, constants and methods, including imported aliases and supported named arguments. Follow facts within one lexical scope and use resolved declarations when available; never infer intent from identifiers or comments.
- D3. Emit one finding per violating operation. Flow facts require a reachable path with no intervening mutation, escaped alias, unknown call involving the tracked value or analysis-budget exhaustion. Uncertain facts cannot prove a violation.

## Exceptions (no report)

- E1. Plus modes, r modes, wrappers with unknown semantics and unknown resources are excluded.
- E2. Exclude shadowed builtin symbols, unresolved required types, incomplete syntax and unsupported PHP versions. Both `@custos-ignore ReadFromWriteOnlyStream` and `@noinspection ReadFromWriteOnlyStream` suppress this inspection.
- E3. A value the shared flow analysis proves is not the failure value at the use is never reported, whatever form the proof takes: a test in an enclosing branch, loop condition or short-circuit operand, an early exit, a statement that leaves on the failing outcome (`$v !== false or exit;`, `$v or throw …;`, `$v ?: throw …;`), a failing branch that ends in a call that never returns (a callee declared `never`, or a function or a final or private method every path of which throws or exits), a test stored in a boolean and tested later while neither the boolean nor the tested variable has been written, and, on PHP 8.0 and later outside any `try` with a `catch`, a builtin call that returned after receiving the value for a parameter that only accepts arrays, objects or callables: such a call throws a `TypeError` for `false`. Positions PHP may skip prove nothing: the right side of `??=`, the arguments of a null-safe call and anything chained after `?->`. A null-safe call to a never-returning method does not end the path, and `f(...)` creates a closure without calling `f`.

## Fix

No automatic fix. Choosing a repair requires runtime information, error-handling policy or a semantic decision.

All edits use exact byte ranges, preserve comments and evaluation order, and require syntax supported by the target PHP version. A fix must never add an evaluation or silently change unrelated arguments.

## PHP versions

Available throughout PHP 5.3–8.5. Apply only where the referenced language features and builtin/extension APIs exist. API-specific later syntax or behavior is gated as described in Detection.

## Options

None. Use ordinary rule configuration to enable or disable this inspection.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "ReadFromWriteOnlyStream": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore ReadFromWriteOnlyStream
```
